page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a compute-focused virtual machine deployed on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 48 physical cores across 48 shared vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz with one thread per core. Memory capacity is configured at 96 GB, establishing a 2 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. Bundled local storage includes 400 GB of SSD capacity, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address. The server profile contains no GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate high multi-core throughput and vector computation capabilities. The instance achieves top-decile performance in stress-ng CPU metrics, Geekbench multi-core evaluation, clang software compilation, and compression routines such as gzip and multi-threaded bzip3. PassMark CPU tests similarly record scores within the top 10 percent. Architectural support covers AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions. Measured memory bandwidth is strong across small and large block operations, while static web serving and Redis throughput remain within upper performance percentiles.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU configuration presents a resource profile oriented around pure compute density rather than large memory buffers. While lightweight model prompt processing benefits from AVX-512 acceleration, token generation speeds are constrained by the absence of dedicated hardware accelerators. This configuration provides qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized batch jobs and compute-intensive microservices. It is functionally suited for CI/CD build runners, parallel code compilation, batch ETL operations, and distributed web serving.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a compute-oriented cloud server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running on the KVM hypervisor. Featuring 48 physical x86_64 cores across 48 vCPUs with a single-thread-per-core configuration, 96 GB of system memory, and 400 GB of bundled local SSD storage, the instance prioritizes raw compute density without GPU acceleration. Benchmark testing places the server in top performance tiers for stress-ng, Geekbench, clang compilation, and parallel compression tasks, supported by hardware AVX-512 and cryptographic extensions. Memory throughput and static web benchmarks demonstrate strong capability, although autoregressive LLM token generation reflects CPU-only limits. The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio delivers an efficient architecture for CPU-bound applications, including continuous integration pipelines, large-scale software builds, batch data transformations, and parallel microservice workloads.
